threepl.simulator

Class SimExprSimpleNode

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.simulator.SimExprSimpleNode
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Constant, SimExprConstants, SimExprNode, SimExprTreeConstants, SimTypes

    public class SimExprSimpleNode
extends java.lang.Object
implements SimExprNode, SimExprConstants, SimExprTreeConstants, SimTypes, Constant
    A SimExprSimpleNode is a node in a SimExpr expression tree. A reference to the root node is obtained with SimExpr.getRoot(). The SimExpr constructors parse the input expression and call a number of SimExprSimpleNode methods on the root node after the parse. Firstly, trim() is called to remove redundant nodes from the tree. A node is redundant where it contains no token and has a single child: it is replaced with the child node. Secondly, resolve() is called to resolve references to threepl identifiers (clocks and variables) and generate values for constant and literal nodes. Thirdly, getType() is called to type check the expression and generate storage for node values where these have not already been created in resolve(). Finally, compressLiteral() is called to replace node sub-trees consisting purely of literal or constant nodes with a single literal node. Once the above process has successfully completed, the expression may be evaluated with the eval() method. eval() returns a SimExpNodeValue object which contains the expression result. Refer SimExpNodeValue for methods to access the value. The expr() method may be called to return the expression String. This will be different to the originally parsed expression String if any literals were removed in compressLiteral().

      • eval

        public SimExprNodeValue eval()
                      throws SimException
        Evaluate node. This is called for the root node (and then recursively for each node in the expression tree) when the expression is evaluated. It must therefore be efficient (avoid memory allocation, unnecessary calls) as breakpoint expressions are evaluated after each simulator clock cycle. Efficiency is not as important for command related nodes as these are not evaluated repetitively while the simulator runs. Should not be called before getType().
        Returns:
        The SimExprNodeValue containing the evaluated value for this node
        Throws:
        SimException - If runtime evaluation error occurs, eg divide by zero

      • reverseChildren

        public void reverseChildren()
        Convert the children[] array into a parent-child tree. The last node in the original children[] becomes the only child. The second last node in the original children[] becomes the first child of this only child, and so on until the first node in the original children[] has become a leaf on the new descendant tree. This method is used to change the tree structure for most binary operator nodes to provide greater efficiency at eval() time.
